He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]]. Cunningham began high school at [[Bowie High School (Arlington, Texas)|Bowie High School]] in his hometown of [[Arlington, Texas]] before transferring to [[Montverde Academy]] in Florida, where he was rated a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and among the top players in the 2020 class by major recruiting services. As a senior, he led one of the best high school teams in history and received [[List of U.S. high school basketball national player of the year awards|national player of the year]] recognition. Cunningham committed to playing college basketball for Oklahoma State, becoming the most heralded recruit to ever do so, and was named a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] and [[Big 12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Big 12 Player of the Year]] after his freshman season with the team. He won a gold medal with the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2019 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]. ==Early life and career== Cunningham was born in [[Arlington, Texas]] to Carrie and Keith Cunningham.{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham |url=https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/c/cunningham-cade.aspx |publisher=[[USA Basketball]] |accessdate=July 1, 2019 |date=June 20, 2019}} He grew up playing [[American football|football]] as a [[quarterback]], which he claims helped become a better passer and leader on the basketball court. Cunningham focused on basketball after watching his brother play the sport in college.{{cite web |last1=Francisco |first1=Alexandra |title=Quarterback of the court: How football helped Cade Cunningham become a 5-star basketball prospect |url=https://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/2019/01/cade_cunningham.html |website=[[The Republican (Springfield, Massachusetts)|The Republican]] |accessdate=July 1, 2019 |date=January 21, 2019}} He frequently played basketball with his father and brother at a [[recreation#Recreation center|recreation center]].{{cite web |last1=Daniels |first1=Evan |title=Cade Cunningham excels with u19 team, talks recruiting |url=https://247sports.com/college/basketball/recruiting/Article/Cade-Cunningham-FIBA-u19-Oklahoma-State-North-Carolina-Duke-133331030/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=July 1, 2019 |date=July 1, 2019}} Cunningham played the [[point guard]] position for Barnett Junior High School in Arlington.{{cite web |last1=Wright |first1=Mark |title=Towering Bowie freshman plays like a standout at age 15 |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/news/local/community/arlington-citizen-journal/article129305124.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |accessdate=July 1, 2019 |date=January 27, 2017}} Since his childhood, he competed for the Texas Titans on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] circuit alongside future [[TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball|TCU]] player [[Mike Miles (basketball)|Mike Miles]].{{cite web |last1=Unruh |first1=Jacob |title=OSU basketball: Cade Cunningham faces unique challenge this week — his close friends |url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/columns/2020/12/16/osu-basketball-cade-cunningham-faces-unique-challenge-this-week-his-close-friends/316893007/ |website=[[The Oklahoman]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=December 15, 2020}} ==High school career== Cunningham attended [[Bowie High School (Arlington, Texas)|Bowie High School]] in Arlington. Soon into his freshman season, he became a starter on the [[varsity team]], which featured [[Kyler Edwards]].{{cite web |last1=Scitt |first1=Marshall |title=Cade Arrives: How an Unlikely No. 1 Recruit Starts a New Era for OSU Hoops |url=https://pistolsfiringblog.com/cade-arrives-how-an-unlikely-no-1-recruit-starts-a-new-era-for-osu-hoops/ |website=Pistols Firing |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=November 25, 2020}} Cunningham averaged 15.2 points, 6.4 rebounds and three assists per game, helping Bowie reach the District 6A Region I final, and was named District 4-6A Newcomer of the Year.{{cite web |last1=Gosset |first1=Brian |title=One of the top basketball prospects in DFW is moving out of state to a national power |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/boys-prep-basketball/article215176365.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |accessdate=July 2, 2019 |date=July 19, 2018}} In December 2017, early in his sophomore season, he suffered an injury while attempting to [[slam dunk|dunk]] at a tournament in [[Houston]].{{cite web |last1=Wright |first1=Mark |title=Why this team isn't freaking out about an injury to its standout sophomore |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/boys-prep-basketball/article190016934.html |website=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |accessdate=July 1, 2019 |date=December 15, 2017}} Cunningham finished the season averaging 18.8 points, 8.2 rebounds, and 5.3 assists per game. He was named District 4-6A co-[[most valuable player]] (MVP) and earned Texas Association of Basketball Coaches All-Region honors.{{cite web |title=2018 SportsDayHS boys basketball All-District lists for area teams |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/03/22/2018-sportsdayhs-boys-basketball-district-lists-area-teams |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=July 2, 2019 |date=March 22, 2018}} [[File:Cade Cunningham.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Cunningham with the Texas Titans at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|EYBL]] in 2019]] Entering his junior year, Cunningham transferred to [[Montverde Academy]], a school in [[Montverde, Florida]] with a successful basketball program. He chose Montverde, whose team was ranked number one in the country by ''[[USA Today]]'', for its academics and coaching.{{cite web |last1=Riddle |first1=Greg |title=Why 5-star basketball recruit Cade Cunningham is leaving Arlington Bowie to join the nation's No. 1 HS team |url=https://sportsday.dallasnews.com/high-school/high-schools/2018/07/20/see-five-star-basketball-recruit-cade-cunningham-leaving-arlington-bowie-join-no-1-high-school-team-nation |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |accessdate=July 2, 2019 |date=July 20, 2018}} On February 2, 2019, Cunningham recorded 26 points, nine assists, and seven rebounds in a 76–51 win against [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]], one of the top high school teams nationally, at the National Hoopfest tournament.{{cite web |last1=Collings |first1=Buddy |title=Montverde beats Oak Hill at Hoopfest in Tampa |url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/sports/highschool/os-sp-hs-bkb-hoopfest-0202-story.html |website=[[Orlando Sentinel]] |accessdate=July 2, 2019 |date=February 2, 2019}} By the end of his junior season, he was averaging 11.4 points, 5.7 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2018-19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Unx8d7lBbEmJkCDKNtEhCw/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=July 2, 2019 |date=April 17, 2019}} Following the high school season, Cunningham was named [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] (EYBL) MVP after averaging 25.1 points, 6.6 rebounds, and 5.2 assists per game for the Texas Titans in the EYBL regular season.{{cite web |title=Nike EYBL Most Valuable Player: Cade Cunningham |url=https://www.d1circuit.com/news_article/show/1031816 |publisher=D1 Circuit |accessdate=August 11, 2019 |date=July 5, 2019}} He was teammates with [[Greg Brown (basketball, born 2001)|Greg Brown]] and Mike Miles with the Titans.{{cite web |last1=Cook |first1=Lyndon |title=Cunningham continues the Texas Titans - Drive Nation summer arms race |url=https://texashoops.rivals.com/news/cunningham-continues-the-texas-titans-drive-nation-summer-arms-race |website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=January 8, 2019}} For his senior season at Montverde, he was joined by many more top recruits, including five-star forwards [[Scottie Barnes]] and [[Day'Ron Sharpe]]. Many analysts regarded his team as one of the best in high school basketball history.{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Ricky |title=Why Montverde is being called the best high school basketball team ever |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2020/1/21/21073999/montverde-basketball-roster-cade-cunningham-scottie-barnes-nba-talent-caleb-houstan |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=January 23, 2020 |date=January 21, 2020}} Cunningham averaged 13.9 points, 6.4 assists and 4.2 rebounds per game, leading Montverde to a 25–0 record with an average margin of victory of 39 points. He played only 22 minutes per game due to the depth of his team.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2019-20 High School Boys Basketball Player of the Year: Cade Cunningham |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Pe--2iLJfkuLqD7ecx_MOA/maxpreps-2019-20-high-school-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year--cade-cunningham.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |accessdate=March 30, 2020 |date=March 25, 2020}} At the end of the season, he was honored as [[Mr. Basketball USA]], [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year Award|Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] and [[MaxPreps National Basketball Player of the Year awards|MaxPreps National Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Nagel |first1=Cody |title=Cade Cunningham earns Naismith Player of the Year honor |url=https://247sports.com/college/oklahoma-state/Article/Oklahoma-State-Cowboys-basketball-recruiting-Cade-Cunningham-earns-Naismith-Player-of-the-Year-144879616/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |accessdate=March 12, 2020 |date=March 11, 2020}} Cunningham was selected to play in the [[2020 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], [[Jordan Brand Classic]] and [[Nike Hoop Summit]], but all three games were canceled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{cite web |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=McDonald's All American Game Cancelled Amid COVID-19 Concerns |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/mcdonalds-all-american-covid19-coronavirus-ncaa-tournament |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |accessdate=March 30, 2020 |date=March 12, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== Cunningham emerged as a top 25 recruit in the 2020 class at the end of his sophomore season at Bowie. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the best players in his class.{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Ricky |title=Cade Cunningham is made for modern basketball |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2019/7/26/8906439/cade-cunningham-recruiting-nba-draft-scouting-report-montverde-high-school |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=August 11, 2019 |date=July 26, 2019}} Cunningham received offers from top [[NCAA Division I]] programs, including [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]], but many analysts viewed [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]] as his likely destination after the program hired his brother, {{ill|Cannen Cunningham|pl|lt=Cannen}}, as an assistant coach.{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham, Montverde Academy, Combo Guard |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Cade-Cunningham-46047476/ |publisher=[[247Sports.com]] |accessdate=August 12, 2019}} On November 5, 2019, Cunningham announced his commitment to Oklahoma State. He became the highest-ranked committed recruit in program history and the first five-star recruit to join Oklahoma State since [[Marcus Smart]] in 2012.{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham commits to Oklahoma State |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/cade-cunningham-commits-oklahoma-state-235824347.html |publisher=[[Yahoo Sports]] |date=November 5, 2019 |accessdate=November 5, 2019}} In June 2020, the NCAA imposed a postseason ban on Oklahoma State. However, Cunningham announced on June 22 that he would still play for the team.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Top recruit Cade Cunningham still going to Oklahoma State despite postseason ban |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29347312/top-recruit-cade-cunningham-going-oklahoma-state-postseason-ban |accessdate=June 22, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=June ==College career== In his college debut for Oklahoma State on November 25, 2020, Cunningham recorded 21 points and 10 rebounds in a 75–68 win over [[UT Arlington Mavericks men's basketball|UT Arlington]].{{cite web |title=Cunningham double-double helps Oklahoma St. top UT Arlington |url=https://okstate.com/news/2020/11/25/mens-basketball-cunningham-double-double-helps-oklahoma-st-top-ut-arlington.aspx |website=[[Oklahoma State Cowboys]] |access-date=November 26, 2020 |date=November 25, 2020}} On December 8, he scored 29 points, including 13 in the final 91 seconds, in an 83–78 victory over [[Oral Roberts Golden Eagles men's basketball|Oral Roberts]].{{cite web |title=Cunningham outduels Abmas, Oklahoma St. beats Oral Roberts |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401261732 |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/watch-oklahoma-state-star-freshman-cade-cunningham-buries-late-game-winning-shot-to-beat-wichita-state/ |website=CBS Sports |access-date=January 26, 2021 |date=December 12, 2020}} On February 27, 2021, he posted a career-high 40 points and 11 rebounds in a 94–90 overtime win against [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]].{{cite web |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=Cade Cunningham powers Oklahoma State's NCAA tournament bid -- but will the Cowboys be allowed in? |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30975498/cade-cunningham-powers-oklahoma-state-ncaa-tournament-bid-cowboys-allowed-in |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=February 28, 2021 Week |url=http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2021/oscar210302.html |publisher=[[United States Basketball Writers Association]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 2, 2021}} Cunningham posted 25 points, eight rebounds and five assists in an 83–74 upset win against top-seeded [[Baylor Bears basketball|Baylor]] in the [[2021 Big 12 Men's Basketball Tournament|Big 12 Tournament]] semifinals on March 12, 2021.{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Oklahoma State stuns Baylor, nears 'vision' of Big 12 men's tournament title |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31054479/oklahoma-state-stuns-baylor-nears-vision-big-12-tournament-title |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 12, 2021}} As a freshman, he averaged 20.1 points, 6.2 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 1.6 steals per game.{{cite web |last1=Rafferty |first1=Scott |title=Potential No. 1 pick Cade Cunningham declares for 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://ca.nba.com/news/potential-no-1-pick-cade-cunningham-declares-for-2021-nba-draft/97bajtm35to01cl35qo2evuy1 |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=April 1, 2021}} After his freshman season, Cunningham was recognized as a consensus first-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]]. He was the first Oklahoma State player to earn the distinction since [[Bob Kurland]] (1944–46).{{cite web |title=Cade Cunningham Collects NABC Award, Named Consensus First Team All-American |url=https://kfor.com/sports/cade-cunningham-collects-nabc-award-named-consensus-first-team-all-american/ |website=[[KFOR-TV]] |access-date=July 16, 2021 |date=March 18, 2021}} He became the fourth [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Michael Beasley]].{{cite web |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=Oklahoma State freshman Cade Cunningham named Big 12 men's hoops player of the year |date=March 8, 2021}} He was unanimously selected to the first-team All-Big 12, the All-Freshman Team and the All-Newcomer Team.{{cite web |title=Cade Earns Big 12 Player, Freshman of the Year Awards,
